blocks.text: Dohra:

Wearing new robes (after being relieved of urinary blockage), The Nawab again started holding his royal court. Declaring that Singhs' prayer had been truly vindicated, As he had confirmed it through his personal experience. (1)
lines: Wearing new robes (after being relieved of urinary blockage),
The Nawab again started holding his royal court.
Declaring that Singhs' prayer had been truly vindicated,
As he had confirmed it through his personal experience.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter inviting Subeg Singh to the royal court, The Nawab honoured him with a seat near his throne. Having experienced the impact of Sikh Gurus' utterings on his own person, He declared the Sikh Gurus and their spiritual words to be true. (2)
lines: Thereafter inviting Subeg Singh to the royal court,
The Nawab honoured him with a seat near his throne.
Having experienced the impact of Sikh Gurus' utterings on his own person,
He declared the Sikh Gurus and their spiritual words to be true.

blocks.text: (Now) he would not mind even if he died the same instant, Death being the inevitable end of every human being born. As he had been relieved of the excruciating pain, The relief followed Subeg Singh's Guru's grace upon him (Nawab). (3)
lines: (Now) he would not mind even if he died the same instant,
Death being the inevitable end of every human being born.
As he had been relieved of the excruciating pain,
The relief followed Subeg Singh's Guru's grace upon him (Nawab).

blocks.text: Would that he would not be subjected to such a torture again, May he shed his mortal frame in peace and comfort. As he had committed oppression upon the Singhs, He had harvested the fruit of his own misdeeds. (4)
lines: Would that he would not be subjected to such a torture again,
May he shed his mortal frame in peace and comfort.
As he had committed oppression upon the Singhs,
He had harvested the fruit of his own misdeeds.

blocks.text: Swearing solemnly on behalf of his own progeny, He promised never to enter into any conflict with the Singhs. Whatever loss of life occurred on the field of battle, Nobody would be held guilty for that loss of life. (5)
lines: Swearing solemnly on behalf of his own progeny,
He promised never to enter into any conflict with the Singhs.
Whatever loss of life occurred on the field of battle,
Nobody would be held guilty for that loss of life.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thereafter, entreating Subeg Singh Jambar, The Nawab asked him for any favour that he wanted. Except for laying a claim to the Nawab's post, Subeg Singh was free to claim everything belonging to his state. (6)
lines: Thereafter, entreating Subeg Singh Jambar,
The Nawab asked him for any favour that he wanted.
Except for laying a claim to the Nawab's post,
Subeg Singh was free to claim everything belonging to his state.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Contemplating deeply over the Nawab's generous offer, Did Subeg Singh wish to do something for Khalsa's welfare. Demanding to be made the chief executive of the state, He asked for a state coin to be struck in his name. (7)
lines: Contemplating deeply over the Nawab's generous offer,
Did Subeg Singh wish to do something for Khalsa's welfare.
Demanding to be made the chief executive of the state,
He asked for a state coin to be struck in his name.

blocks.text: Accepting Subeg Singh's proposals in totality, Did the Nawab appoint Subeg Singh as the chief executive. Full well had Subeg Singh known (Bhai Taru Singh's prophesy), That the Nawab would not live beyond one or two days. (8)
lines: Accepting Subeg Singh's proposals in totality,
Did the Nawab appoint Subeg Singh as the chief executive.
Full well had Subeg Singh known (Bhai Taru Singh's prophesy),
That the Nawab would not live beyond one or two days.

blocks.text: Wasting, therefore, no time in getting his proposals implemented, Subeg Singh got a state coin struck in his own name. Bearing an inscription of his own name Subeg Singh Jambar, He made this coin and his writ run over the entire state. (9)
lines: Wasting, therefore, no time in getting his proposals implemented,
Subeg Singh got a state coin struck in his own name.
Bearing an inscription of his own name Subeg Singh Jambar,
He made this coin and his writ run over the entire state.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The gallows that the Nawab had installed for Singhs' execution, Did Subeg Singh order the same to be dismantled. The Mussoleums that had been raised over Sikh martyr's bodies, Did Subeg Singh dismantle and cremate the martyrs last remains. (10)
lines: The gallows that the Nawab had installed for Singhs' execution,
Did Subeg Singh order the same to be dismantled.
The Mussoleums that had been raised over Sikh martyr's bodies,
Did Subeg Singh dismantle and cremate the martyrs last remains.

blocks.text: Hardly had a time of four days passed, As the Nawab had lived in peace and bliss. Thereafter suddenly did the Nawab pass away, Without having undergone any pain or discomfort. (11)
lines: Hardly had a time of four days passed,
As the Nawab had lived in peace and bliss.
Thereafter suddenly did the Nawab pass away,
Without having undergone any pain or discomfort.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Having passed through the whole ordeal for twenty-two days, Did the Nawab's soul depart forever on a longish journey. Amidst the cries of sudden wailing and weeping (in Nawab's household), Did the people hail Nawab's death as a good riddance. (12)
lines: Having passed through the whole ordeal for twenty-two days,
Did the Nawab's soul depart forever on a longish journey.
Amidst the cries of sudden wailing and weeping (in Nawab's household),
Did the people hail Nawab's death as a good riddance.

blocks.text: With the Hindus feeling heartened at the oppressor's death, Truly had the Guru vindicated His devout Sikhs' honour. With Bhai Taru Singh's solemn pledge having been fulfilled, Really had a wave of happiness run over the Singhs' camp. (13)
lines: With the Hindus feeling heartened at the oppressor's death,
Truly had the Guru vindicated His devout Sikhs' honour.
With Bhai Taru Singh's solemn pledge having been fulfilled,
Really had a wave of happiness run over the Singhs' camp.

blocks.text: Muslims having fallen in the grip of fear and grief, They apprehended India's sovereignty slipping from their grip. With the Muslims' hold over India having gone weak, The Khalsa Panth's stock went high in the region. (14)
lines: Muslims having fallen in the grip of fear and grief,
They apprehended India's sovereignty slipping from their grip.
With the Muslims' hold over India having gone weak,
The Khalsa Panth's stock went high in the region.

blocks.text: It was in the year seventeen hundred and Ninety-one1 , That Hakikat Rai's murder had made no impact on the Mughal rule. It was indeed to Bhai Taru Singh's credit to win that glory, That he had decimated the Nawab with shoe-beatings. (15)
lines: It was in the year seventeen hundred and Ninety-one1 ,
That Hakikat Rai's murder had made no impact on the Mughal rule.
It was indeed to Bhai Taru Singh's credit to win that glory,
That he had decimated the Nawab with shoe-beatings.

blocks.text: Thus remained the honour of the Khalsa Panth intact, Thus were the Mughals disgraced and dishonoured. Thus did Bhai Taru Singh and Bhai Subeg Singh, Rendered a great service to the Sikh Panth. (16)
lines: Thus remained the honour of the Khalsa Panth intact,
Thus were the Mughals disgraced and dishonoured.
Thus did Bhai Taru Singh and Bhai Subeg Singh,
Rendered a great service to the Sikh Panth.
